data.Documented value: Digital Banking Era Organizational Culture as a Leader Driver in Digital Banking: The Case of the Uttarakhand Private Banks.

In the modern digital banking company – leadership is as much about culture as it is direct reporting lines. Driven by rapidly changing technology, increasing competition and the needs of group clients, private sector banks have been forced to revisit leadership styles and internal cultural architecture. In that kind of environment, making your leaders in the same mindset is not only about tech knowledge but also trusting and collaboration working, ethics and innovation. The paper under study overlooks at how the organisational culture through the OCTAPACE cultural model determines impact of on leadership effectiveness in private banks operating in Uttarakhand. The OCTAPACE model has a holistic perspective in understanding behaviour and culture, related to leadership and performance which stands for: openness, confrontation, trust authenticity autonomy (independence) pro-action (change) collaboration excerpts. The study is proposed to be a quantitative work of research conducted on primary data from employees (both managerial and operative level) of selected private banks of Uttarakhand. Organizational culture and leadership effectiveness were assessed by a structured questionnaire for the participants. The study followed descriptive research design and utilized the correlation analysis (Pearson’s r) to understand the influence of OCTAPACE dimensions on leadership in digital rejuvenating banking sectors. Cultural clustering - trust, autonomy, collaboration and pro- action are highlighted as key cultural clusters which have considerable predictive power for the effectiveness of leadership. Leaders who work in supportive and adaptive cultures are more agile, ethical, engaged of their people and innovative. This study contributes to the OB literature by considering organisational culture as an empirically established antecedent of leadership in digital banking age. In theoretical terms, findings offer some implications for banks who wish to attain environmental sustainability from a long-term orientation through enhancing human-cantered culture development not only as the enabler of technological improvement.

Using a quantitative research approach, structured surveys will be deployed to dissect various facets of consumer engagement with digital banking. The study will scrutinize levels of awareness, frequency of usage, satisfaction levels, perceived benefits, and risks associated with Standard Bank Ltd's e-banking platforms. Additionally, it seeks to identify factors influencing consumers' adoption of digital banking services and explore the interplay between perceived benefits, risks, and consumer behavior. Insights gleaned from this research are poised to provide invaluable guidance for Standard Bank Ltd and other banking institutions. By understanding consumers' evolving needs and expectations, tailored digital banking offerings can be crafted to enhance customer satisfaction and experience. Moreover, the study's findings will inform strategic decision-making processes and drive initiatives aimed at optimizing customer engagement strategies. In summary, this study contributes to the evolving discourse on e-banking and consumer behavior. It paints a nuanced portrait of consumer perceptions towards digital banking services in Bangladesh, with Standard Bank Ltd serving as a focal point for exploration. Through empirical analysis and insights, it charts a course toward a more customer-centric approach in the realm of digital banking.

data.Documented value: Navigating Digital Inequality: Examining Factors Affecting Rural Customers’ Internet Banking Adoption in Post-COVID Bangladesh
International Journal of Business and Technology Management

As the world continues to navigate the new normal brought about by the COVID-19 pandemic, one issue that has come to the forefront is digital inequality. In Bangladesh, where a significant portion of the population resides in rural areas, the adoption of internet banking has been hindered by various factors. However, understanding these factors is crucial, especially now that digital transactions have become more important. This study aims to understand the factors influencing the adoption of internet banking services among rural customers in Bangladesh. To acquire data, a questionnaire was administered to 443 rural bank customers in the district of Barisal. The Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) revealed three primary factors: trust compatibility, service benefit, and access to consumer education. In addition, the research sought to determine if the identified factors, particularly access to consumer education, varied according to the occupation and income level of rural consumers. Using exhaustive Chi-squared Automatic Interaction Detection (CHAID) analysis, the findings revealed that access to consumer education differs significantly by occupation level, with business and service holders being more likely than farmers to have access to consumer education. This research contributes to the literature by providing insights into the adoption of internet banking by rural customers and informing policymakers about the special needs of this demographic.

sections.heading: E-Banking: Consumer Perception Towards Digital Banking With Reference to Standard
paragraphs: Bangladesh, a nation deeply rooted in traditional banking practices, is gradually embracing the digital revolution. The country's financial landscape is undergoing a transformative shift, with the introduction of digital banking services. This evolution is not just a technological advancement but a strategic move to enhance customer experience and streamline financial transactions. However, as with any significant change, there are mixed perceptions among the populace. [[S2|Qeios]]

[[S2|Qeios]] Consumer perception towards digital banking in Bangladesh is complex and multifaceted. On one hand, there is a growing awareness and acceptance of digital banking services. This suggests a positive trend towards digital adoption, driven by the convenience and accessibility offered by these services. [[S2|Qeios]] However, the study also highlights that while awareness is increasing, actual usage is still relatively low.

Only 20% of the population has used digital banking services, indicating a need for greater engagement and education. This discrepancy between awareness and usage underscores the importance of effective marketing and education campaigns to encourage widespread adoption. [[S2|Qeios]] When it comes to the perception of benefits and risks associated with digital banking, the findings are mixed. On one hand, respondents express satisfaction with the convenience and speed of digital transactions.

This satisfaction is driven by the ability to access information and perform transactions anytime and anywhere. [[S2|Qeios]] On the other hand, there is a significant concern about security and privacy. This highlights the need for robust security measures and transparent communication to build trust among consumers. [[S2|Qeios]] Moreover, the study identifies factors influencing consumer behavior towards digital banking.

Age and income levels play a crucial role. Younger generations and those with higher incomes are more likely to adopt digital banking services due to their familiarity with technology and the convenience it offers. This suggests that targeted marketing strategies should focus on younger demographics and those with higher disposable incomes. [[S2|Qeios]] In terms of the mechanism of adoption, the study indicates that peer influence and social proof play a significant role.

Users are more likely to try digital banking services when they see their friends or family members using them. This suggests that community engagement and word-of-mouth recommendations can be powerful tools in promoting digital adoption. [[S2|Qeios]] However, the study also points out that digital banking services are not without challenges. The high cost of digital infrastructure and the need for skilled personnel to manage and secure digital transactions are significant barriers.

This highlights the need for financial institutions to invest in technology and training to ensure that these services are accessible and reliable. [[S2|Qeios]] In conclusion, while Bangladesh is moving towards a digital banking future, there is still a long way to go. The study underscores the importance of education, security measures, and community engagement in fostering widespread adoption.

sections.heading: Job-related Factors and Satisfaction of Bank Employees on Digital Banking
paragraphs: Bangladesh's banking sector is rapidly evolving, driven by advancements in the ICT sector. This research aims to identify significant job-related factors that affect job satisfaction among bank employees in Bangladesh. A survey questionnaire, adapted from the University of Minnesota's MSQ instrument, was used to determine the levels of satisfaction among 414 bank employees working at four Bangladeshi public commercial banks and four private commercial banks. The statistical techniques utilized include reliability tests, exploratory factor analysis, and confirmatory factor analysis to analyze the data.

[[S4|Selangor Business Review]] The findings indicate that motivators and hygiene factors are the most significant factors that contribute to job satisfaction among bank employees. Motivators include recognition, growth opportunities, and fair treatment, while hygiene factors include good working conditions, adequate compensation, and job security. The study suggests that there is a positive relationship among motivators, hygiene factors, and other job-related factors with the satisfaction of employees. [[S4|Selangor Business Review]] In the context of job-related factors, motivators such as recognition and growth opportunities are crucial for job satisfaction.

For example, employees who feel valued and appreciated are more likely to be satisfied with their work. Similarly, growth opportunities, such as training and development programs, can also contribute to job satisfaction. Hygiene factors, on the other hand, include good working conditions, adequate compensation, and job security. For instance, employees who feel that their work environment is conducive to their well-being and that they are adequately compensated for their efforts are more likely to be satisfied with their job.

[[S4|Selangor Business Review]] The research also suggests that there is a positive relationship between job satisfaction and other job-related factors. For example, employees who feel that their work is meaningful and that they are making a positive impact on the organization are more likely to be satisfied with their job. Similarly, employees who feel that they have a good working relationship with their colleagues and that they are able to communicate effectively with them are more likely to be satisfied with their job. [[S4|Selangor Business Review]] In conclusion, the research suggests that job satisfaction among bank employees in Bangladesh is influenced by a range of job-related factors.

Motivators such as recognition, growth opportunities, and fair treatment are crucial for job satisfaction, while hygiene factors such as good working conditions, adequate compensation, and job security are also important.

paragraphs: Bangladesh needs digital banking, but not more. While digital banking is crucial for the country's financial landscape, it should be approached with a balanced perspective. The findings indicate that while digital banking can enhance efficiency and customer experience, it does not significantly improve financial performance or operational efficiency.

sections.heading: Effect of E-Banking on Banking Sector of Bangladesh
paragraphs: Bangladesh, a nation with a rapidly growing digital economy, is increasingly embracing the benefits of digital banking. The concept of e-banking has been gaining traction, offering numerous advantages such as reduced transaction times, enhanced security, and increased convenience. However, the implementation of e-banking in Bangladesh has not been without challenges. One of the primary concerns is the security of e-banking transactions, which has been a significant issue in the country.

[[S2|International Journal of Economics Finance and]] Despite the advancements in technology, the security measures in place have not been sufficient to protect the sensitive information of users. [[S2|International Journal of Economics Finance and]] The study conducted by S9 on the impact of e-banking on the banking sector of Bangladesh has provided valuable insights into the practices and impacts of e-banking in the country. The research involved the selection of 120 bankers and bank customers from various divisions, districts, towns, and rural areas of Bangladesh. The sample was purposively chosen to ensure a diverse representation of the population.

Statistical tools such as SPSS were used to analyze the data collected from the participants. [[S2|International Journal of Economics Finance and]] The major findings of the study indicate that e-banking requires a minimum workforce compared to traditional banking. This is due to the automation of many banking processes, which reduces the need for human intervention. Additionally, e-banking has significantly reduced the need for carrying cash, as customers can now make transactions through digital channels.

Cards are used for shopping, further reducing the need for physical cash. The study also highlights that there is no need to maintain huge documents for banking functions in e-banking, making it more efficient and convenient for customers. [[S2|International Journal of Economics Finance and]] However, one of the significant challenges faced by e-banking in Bangladesh is the security of transactions. The study points out that despite the advancements in technology, the security measures in place have not been sufficient to protect the sensitive information of users.

This has led to a feeling of insecurity among customers, particularly when it comes to withdrawing and depositing money from ATM booths. The study also mentions that all the ATM booths of Bangladeshi banks are not in safe positions, which adds to the concerns of customers. [[S2|International Journal of Economics Finance and]] The findings of this study are crucial for the banking sector in Bangladesh, as it provides a clear understanding of the practices and impacts of e-banking.

sections.heading: PRESENT AND FUTURE OF DIGITAL BANKING SERVICES IN BANGLADESH
paragraphs: Bangladesh has seen a remarkable transformation in its financial sector, particularly in the realm of digital banking. The rapid digitalization of the sector has positioned Mobile Financial Services (MFSs) as a cornerstone of financial inclusion and socio-economic empowerment. This study explores the evolution, barriers, and impacts of MFS adoption across households and small to medium enterprises (SMEs) in Bangladesh, employing a qualitative research design to capture the multifaceted experiences and insights of key industry professionals. The interpretivist framework guided the study, emphasizing the subjective understanding of participants actively engaged in the MFS ecosystem.

For PRESENT AND FUTURE OF DIGITAL BANKING SERVICES IN, [[S3|OpenAlex research index]] [[S3|OpenAlex research index]] Data were collected through semi-structured, in-depth interviews with five senior experts representing leading financial institutions, regulatory authorities, and fintech organizations. For PRESENT AND FUTURE OF DIGITAL BANKING SERVICES IN, the selection of participants followed a purposive sampling approach, ensuring that each respondent possessed over a decade of experience in policy implementation, digital finance operations, or regulatory oversight. For PRESENT AND FUTURE OF DIGITAL BANKING SERVICES IN, the research findings were derived through Braun and Clarke’s (2006) six-phase thematic analysis, which enabled the systematic identification of recurring themes such as technological accessibility, digital literacy, regulatory complexity, trust, and socio-economic empowerment. For PRESENT AND FUTURE OF DIGITAL BANKING SERVICES IN, the analysis revealed that while Bangladesh has achieved substantial progress in digital financial inclusion—accounting for nearly 12% of the global mobile money accounts (The Daily Star, 2024)—challenges such as high transaction fees, limited rural connectivity, and cybersecurity concerns persist.

For PRESENT AND FUTURE OF DIGITAL BANKING SERVICES IN, [[S3|OpenAlex research index]] MFS platforms like bKash, Rocket, and Nagad have redefined household and business financial practices by enabling faster remittances, transparent transactions, and enhanced liquidity management. For PRESENT AND FUTURE OF DIGITAL BANKING SERVICES IN, at the same time, gender disparities and digital literacy gaps continue to hinder the equitable distribution of benefits, highlighting the need for targeted financial education and regulatory reform. For PRESENT AND FUTURE OF DIGITAL BANKING SERVICES IN, this study contributes to the growing body of literature on digital financial transformation in developing economies by offering grounded insights into how MFS reshapes Bangladesh’s socio-economic fabric. For PRESENT AND FUTURE OF DIGITAL BANKING SERVICES IN, the findings underscore the importance of balancing innovation with inclusive policy frameworks to ensure sustainability and trust within the digital financial ecosystem.

[[S3|OpenAlex research index]] The research advocates for a multi-dimensional strategy that includes a mix of technological advancements, accessible financial education, and regulatory reforms to address the unique challenges faced by rural customers. The study also emphasizes the need for continuous monitoring and adaptation to keep up with the evolving digital landscape, ensuring that the benefits of digital financial services reach all segments of the population.
